# 04 — Schedule & Playoffs

## 4.1 Regular Season

**Weeks 1–14.** Fourteen head-to-head matchups.

**No divisions.** All twelve teams sit in one table. Each team plays eleven opponents once and three opponents twice.

This matters more in dynasty than it would in redraft: the standings are a clean ranking of 1 through 12, and that ranking directly sets the [rookie draft order](06-rookie-draft.md#62-draft-order). No team backs into the playoffs off a weak division, and no 6-8 division winner distorts next spring's draft.

**Scheduling.** The schedule is generated by Sleeper before Week 1 and is not adjusted afterward.

## 4.2 Playoffs

**Weeks 15, 16, and 17.** Six teams. The top two seeds receive a first-round bye.

| Round | Week | Matchups | Decides |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wild card | 15 | 3 v 6, 4 v 5 | Who advances |
| Semifinal | 16 | 1 v lowest remaining seed, 2 v other | Who plays for the title |
| **5th place game** | 16 | The two wild card losers | 5th/6th place and **picks 1.07 / 1.08** |
| Championship | 17 | Semifinal winners | Champion and runner-up |
| **3rd place game** | 17 | The two semifinal losers | 3rd/4th place and **picks 1.09 / 1.10** |

**Nobody's season ends early.** Every playoff team plays all three weeks. Lose in the wild card round and you are still playing in Week 16 with a draft pick on the line; lose in the semifinal and you are still playing in Week 17. There is no week in which a playoff team has nothing to play for, which is the entire reason the placement games exist.

**The winner of a placement game gets the better pick.** This is the opposite of the usual convention, and it is deliberate. If the loser of the 5th place game took 1.07, the game would be worth losing and we would have built a tanking incentive into the postseason on purpose. Winning is rewarded at every stage, so a complete lineup is always in your interest as well as required by [§9.3](09-governance-and-conduct.md#93-tanking-and-lineup-integrity).

Placement games use the same tiebreakers as any playoff game (§4.4).

**Why week 17 and not week 18.** NFL teams rest starters in Week 18. Ending the fantasy season in Week 17 is now near-universal and this league does the same.

**Reseeding** happens after the wild card round: the highest remaining seed always plays the lowest remaining seed.

**Playoff seeding** is by regular-season standings, with ties broken per §4.3.

**No single-week reseeding of byes.** Byes are locked to seeds 1 and 2 at the end of Week 14.

## 4.3 Standings Tiebreakers

Applied in order until the tie is broken:

1. **Head-to-head record** (only if the tied teams played, and only if it is decisive among all tied teams)
2. **Total points scored**
3. **Total points against** (lower is better)
4. **Best single-week score**
5. **Coin flip by the commissioner**, conducted publicly in the league chat

If more than two teams are tied, apply each step to the whole group; when the group splits, restart the sequence for the remaining tied teams.

## 4.4 Ties

**Regular season:** a matchup tied to the hundredth of a point is recorded as a tie (0.5 win, 0.5 loss).

**Playoffs:** ties are broken by, in order:

1. Higher regular-season seed
2. Higher regular-season points scored

There are no bench-points or overtime tiebreakers. The higher seed earned the tiebreak during the season.

## 4.5 The Toilet Bowl

The six teams that miss the playoffs play a **toilet bowl** in weeks 15–17. It is not a consolation bracket. **Losers advance.** Win a game and you are out; lose and you move one round closer to the **Willie Barron Trophy - Brought to you by The Pitch**, which is awarded to the team that loses the toilet bowl final.

**Seeding** is by regular-season finish — seed 7 is the best non-playoff team, seed 12 the worst. The bracket mirrors the playoff bracket, inverted: where the two best teams in the league get a bye that helps them, the two worst get a bye that pushes them toward the trophy.

| Round | Week | Matchups | Who advances |
|---|---|---|---|
| First round | 15 | 7 v 10, 8 v 9 | The **losers**. Seeds 11 and 12 have byes. |
| Semifinal | 16 | 12 v highest remaining seed, 11 v other | The **losers** |
| Toilet Bowl final | 17 | The two remaining teams | The **loser** takes the Willie Barron Trophy - Brought to you by The Pitch |

A team that wins its first toilet bowl game is finished for the season. Its escape is complete and it plays no further meaningful games.

**You must still field a complete, legal, healthy lineup every week.** This is the part that makes the toilet bowl work rather than turning it into a farce. [§9.3](09-governance-and-conduct.md#93-tanking-and-lineup-integrity) applies in full through Week 17: you may not bench a healthy starter, start a player on bye, or leave a slot empty in order to lose. Sitting your best players to chase the trophy carries the same penalties as sitting them to chase a draft pick.

The result is that nobody can steer the outcome. You field your real team, and whether you take the trophy home is decided by three weeks of scoring you do not control. That is the joke, and it only lands if everyone is genuinely trying to win.

**The toilet bowl does not determine the rookie draft order.** Picks 1.01–1.06 are locked by regular-season finish at the end of Week 14 and nothing in weeks 15–17 moves them — see [Rookie Draft §6.2](06-rookie-draft.md#62-draft-order). This is deliberate and important. If the toilet bowl set the draft order, every team in it would be trying to lose games that also decide their draft position, which is the exact problem the draft-order rule exists to solve.

This is the opposite arrangement from the playoff side, and for the opposite reason. Playoff teams have their picks decided by [placement games](#42-playoffs) because those games reward winning; the toilet bowl rewards winning too, but by letting you *escape* rather than by paying you a draft slot. Both halves of the league spend weeks 15–17 trying to win. Neither half can improve its draft position by losing.

**A note on the incentives.** The toilet bowl quietly works against regular-season tanking. Finishing 12th gets you the 1.01, but it also gets you a bye straight into the toilet bowl semifinal and two games from the Willie Barron Trophy - Brought to you by The Pitch. Tanking now has a price attached, paid in front of the whole league.

**Running the bracket.** Sleeper's consolation bracket advances winners, which is the opposite of this. The commissioner posts the toilet bowl bracket in the group text before Week 15 and tracks it by hand from Sleeper's weekly scores. Where the platform's display and this section disagree, this section governs.
